sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles a short stretch of the southern Apennines between the Basilicata and Calabria regions, across of the Coscile R. valley, on the southern flank of Mt. Pollino. This source is a high-angle, SW-dipping, normal fault system along the main extensional axis of the southern Apennines.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Pondrelli et al., 2006; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show a virtual lack of seismicity in this region, except the 26 January 1708 (Mw 5.6, Pollino) earthquake, that has occurred just north of the area.
This Source shows the polarity switch between the NE-dipping, greater NW-SE striking extensional axis of the southern Apennines (to the north), and the ca. W-dipping normal fault system that departs from the southern flank of Mt. Pollino through the western shoulder of the Sila massif.
Paleoseismological data by Cinti et al (1997, 2002) allowed to describe the Castrovillari normal fault, that forms the core of this source, The same authors believe that the Pollino Fault, to the north of this source, acts as a structurally barrier to the N-ward propagation of the Castrovillari fault. In an area with such a rare seismicity (a fact that could also be due to earthquake recurrence times longer than the historical catalogue's time span), such consideration about fault size can be crucial when it comes to estimate maximum expected magnitude.
The main segment of this Source has been recognized for its seismogenic potential. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this source was based on that of the mapped structures. The dip was based on geological data and geometrical considerations. The rake represents pure extension, based on geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological data. The slip rate was based on paleoseismological data.
